datasets.title: Algeria - Densité des foyers d'incendies dans les wilayas de Bejaia et Tizi Ouzou entre le 11 et le 13 août 2021
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FR20210811DZA Cette carte illustre la densité des foyers d'incendies détectés à partir des données VIIRS acquise entre le 11 et le 13 août 2021. Les wilayas de Bejaia, Tizi Ouzou et Ain-Defla semblent compter le plus grand nombre de foyers d'incendie avec respectivement 1,080; 573 et 190. En se basant sur les données démographique Worldpop, environ 70,000 personnes dans la wilaya de Tizi Ouzou; 25,000 personnes dans la wilaya de Bejaia et 13,000 personnes dans la wilaya de Skikda vivent à proximité des foyers d'incendie. Ceci est une analyse préliminaire et n'as pas encore été validée sur le terrain. Ne pas hésiter à envoyer vos commentaires au Centre Satellitaire des Nations Unies (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/densite-des-foyers-d-incendies-dans-les-wilayas-de-bejaia-et-tizi-ouzou-entre-le-11-et-le-]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed VIIRS satellite imagery acquired between August 11-13, 2021 to detect and map active wildfire hotspots in three Algerian wilayas. Hotspot density was calculated by administrative boundary, and population exposure was estimated by intersecting hotspot locations with WorldPop gridded demographic data to quantify residents in proximity to fires.
